introduction_markdown: CAMEROON GENERAL CERTIFICATE OF EDUCATION BOARD, General Certificate of Education Examination, June 2020, Ordinary Level, Additional Mathematics, Paper 2 (0575). Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL QUESTIONS IN SECTION A and ANY TWO QUESTIONS FROM EITHER SECTION B or SECTION C. IN SECTIONS B AND C, ALL QUESTIONS CARRY EQUAL MARKS. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C but NOT a combination of all three. Section A: Pure Mathematics (compulsory, answer all questions). Section B: Mechanics (if this section is chosen, then Section C may not be chosen; answer any two questions). Section C: Statistics and Probability (if this section is chosen, then Section B may not be chosen; answer any two questions). All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Electronic calculators may be used. Where necessary take g as 10 m s^-2. Formulae Booklets may be used.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Given that $(x+1)$ is a factor of $f(x)$, where $f(x)=2x^3+3x^2+kx+2$,

(a) Find the value of $k$. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Since $(x+1)$ is a factor of $f(x)$, the factor theorem gives $f(-1)=0$.

$$f(-1)=2(-1)^3+3(-1)^2+k(-1)+2=-2+3-k+2=3-k.$$

Setting $3-k=0$ gives

**$k=3$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) With this value of $k$, show that $f(x)=(x+1)(2x^2+x+2)$. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
With $k=3$ we have $f(x)=2x^3+3x^2+3x+2$. Expand the right-hand side:

$$(x+1)(2x^2+x+2)=2x^3+x^2+2x+2x^2+x+2=2x^3+3x^2+3x+2=f(x).$$

(Equivalently, divide $f(x)$ by $(x+1)$: the quotient is $2x^2+x+2$ and the remainder is $0$.) Hence $f(x)=(x+1)(2x^2+x+2)$, as required.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(ii) Given also that $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the roots of the equation $x^2+x+2=0$.

(a) Find the values of $\alpha+\beta$ and $\alpha\beta$. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
For $ax^2+bx+c=0$ the sum of the roots is $-\dfrac{b}{a}$ and the product is $\dfrac{c}{a}$. Here $a=1$, $b=1$, $c=2$, so

**$\alpha+\beta=-1$ and $\alpha\beta=2$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) Hence, write down another quadratic equation with integral coefficients whose roots are $-\alpha$ and $-\beta$. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
For the new roots $-\alpha$ and $-\beta$:

- sum $=(-\alpha)+(-\beta)=-(\alpha+\beta)=-(-1)=1$;
- product $=(-\alpha)(-\beta)=\alpha\beta=2$.

A quadratic with sum of roots $S$ and product of roots $P$ is $x^2-Sx+P=0$. So

$$x^2-x+2=0.$$

The coefficients $1,-1,2$ are integers, as required. **The equation is $x^2-x+2=0$.** (Check: replacing $x$ by $-x$ in $x^2+x+2=0$ gives $x^2-x+2=0$.)
